decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1: “Save a bookmark … add a link.”
decisions.note: The baseline included URL-based bookmark creation, conforming to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 offered only “auto-derive a title”; client entry 2 required collection of “page title, description, site icon, and preview image.”
decisions.note: At the initial specification gate, metadata capture omitted three required metadata fields; the client supplied them.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 described an optional title and generic editing; client entry 2 required collected title and description to remain editable.
decisions.note: The initial specification did not establish editable auto-collected title and description; the client added the requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 listed unspecified “duplicate handling”; client entry 2 said an existing address must open for updating “rather than merely warning me.” Maker entry 3 confirms the prior behavior was “just warning.”
decisions.note: The initial duplicate-save behavior contradicted the required convergence on editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 only said “Browse”; client entry 2 required the list to emphasize “title, description, tags, and site icon.”
decisions.note: The readability-first fields were absent from the initial presented scope and were supplied by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1: “Browse, search & reopen … open the original page.”
decisions.note: Opening the original URL conformed to the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1: “Edit & delete … remove bookmarks, with delete confirmation.”
decisions.note: Permanent bookmark deletion was included.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1: “Organize with tags — label bookmarks and filter by tag.”
decisions.note: Tag assignment and specific-tag filtering were present at the baseline gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 presented tag labeling/filtering without suggestions; client entry 2 requested “Suggestions from existing tags while entering tags.”
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete was missing from the baseline scope and added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 offered “search by keyword”; client entry 2 required search across “titles, descriptions, notes, addresses, and tags, without caring about capitalization.”
decisions.note: The client expanded the underspecified keyword search to the required fields and case-insensitive behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 offered only keyword search; client entry 2 requested “Exact phrases, `#tag` searches, and combinations such as AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.”
decisions.note: Advanced search syntax was absent and explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 offered keyword search; client entry 2 requested Boolean operators but did not state the reference rule that quoted operators must be searchable as literals.
decisions.note: The quoted-operator subrule was still absent after the initial response; it was surfaced only at the next specification review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 contained no note capability; client entry 2 requested “Descriptions and notes, including formatted notes.”
decisions.note: Formatted bookmark notes were added at the initial specification review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted read state; client entry 2 requested “Read-later/read status and a separate unread view.”
decisions.note: The client supplied unread/read state and the unread perspective.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted archiving; client entry 2 requested “Archiving as a reversible action, with archived items excluded from normal browsing and search.”
decisions.note: The response added reversible archiving and distinguished it from permanent deletion.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted archiving entirely; client entry 2 requested reversible archiving and exclusion from normal browsing but did not explicitly require a separate archive-only list.
decisions.note: The distinct archive-list requirement was not expressly surfaced in the initial correction.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted bulk operations; client entry 2 requested selecting several bookmarks or “everything matching the current search or filter” for tagging, read state, archiving, and deletion.
decisions.note: Both selected-item and complete-filter bulk actions were supplied by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted sorting; client entry 2 requested “Sorting the bookmark list.”
decisions.note: List sorting was added at the initial review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 had only Bookmark and Tag entities; client entry 2 requested reusable combinations of searches and included/excluded tags.
decisions.note: Saved filter bundles were absent and supplied by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted preservation; client entry 2 requested a local page copy, PDF-file preservation, and an Internet Archive option.
decisions.note: The response added both local and Internet Archive preservation.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted preservation; client entry 2 asked for a “local copy” but did not specify the reference requirement that a web page be stored as one self-contained HTML file.
decisions.note: The single-file HTML constraint remained unexpressed until round 2.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted interchange; client entry 2 requested importing and exporting standard browser bookmark files while retaining titles, tags, and dates.
decisions.note: Import and export were added with the required retained fields.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 1/round 1 omitted profile preferences; client entry 2 requested default sorting, items shown, and text size.
decisions.note: Display-related settings were supplied by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presented duplicate saves opening the existing bookmark and metadata capture of title, description, icon, and preview image with editable title/description.
decisions.note: The revision-2 decisions conformed to the corrected metadata and duplicate requirements.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presented tag suggestions and case-insensitive search across title, description, note, address, and tags, including phrases and `#tag`.
decisions.note: These revision-2 search and autocomplete behaviors conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presented “AND/OR/NOT with parentheses” without the literal-word rule; client entry 4 required that AND, OR, and NOT remain searchable as ordinary words when quoted.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing operator-quoting rule at the revision-2 review.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Read/unread status + separate unread view.”
decisions.note: The presented read-state behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2: “Reversible archiving, excluded from normal browsing/search.”
decisions.note: Reversible archive semantics and ordinary-search exclusion conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 described reversible archiving and normal-search exclusion but did not say whether an archive-only list existed; client entry 4 did not address that point.
decisions.note: At this specification stage the transcript cannot establish conformance or divergence for the separate archive view.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presented bulk actions with select-all matching, sorting, and saved views combining search with included/excluded tags.
decisions.note: The revision-2 presentation covered these organization behaviors consistently with the reference at the stated level.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 offered a generic “local copy”; client entry 4 required “a self-contained HTML file” while retaining PDFs as PDFs.
decisions.note: The local-page representation was underspecified and corrected to the required single-file HTML behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 explicitly presented PDF-file download and an Internet Archive option.
decisions.note: The PDF and Internet Archive preservation decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 presented standard browser bookmark import/export retaining titles, tags, and dates, plus default sort, page size, and text size settings.
decisions.note: These revision-2 decisions conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 stated only title/description editing; client entry 4 required editing the bookmark address as well as title, description, tags, and note.
decisions.note: The editable URL field was missing and explicitly corrected.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 emphasized `#tag` search and list tags; client entry 4 said selecting a visible tag must directly filter the list and that typing `#tag` was insufficient.
decisions.note: The client corrected the interaction to direct tag selection.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 proposed ignoring “stray fragment/tracking params” for duplicate detection; client entry 4 rejected wholesale removal because either can identify different content and limited removal to known destination-preserving cases.
decisions.note: Overbroad normalization could merge distinct URLs, so the client supplied a reference-compatible matching rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 proposed new bookmarks defaulting to unread; client entry 4 explicitly said “The unread default … [is] fine.”
decisions.note: Defaulting new bookmarks to unread is compatible with read-later support.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 3/round 2 proposed a basic safe formatting set; client entry 4 said “safe note formatting [is] fine.”
decisions.note: Safe rendered formatting is compatible with the formatted-note requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 added editable address behavior; client entry 6 approved revision 3.
decisions.note: The revised edit behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 added “clicking a tag shown on a bookmark immediately filters the list”; client entry 6 approved.
decisions.note: The revised tag interaction conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 stated quoted AND/OR/NOT are ordinary search text; client entry 6 approved.
decisions.note: The revised Boolean literal rule conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 specified one self-contained HTML file with embedded assets and PDFs stored as PDFs; client entry 6 approved.
decisions.note: The revised local-preservation format conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 5/round 3 limited normalization to host case, default ports, a trailing slash, and maintained known-harmless cases while otherwise preserving fragments and query parameters; client entry 6 approved.
decisions.note: The revised duplicate-matching rule no longer conflated potentially distinct destinations.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 selected a custom parser for phrase/tag/Boolean search, a safe note sanitizer, and Playwright-based self-contained preservation.
decisions.note: These plan-level implementation choices were functionally consistent with the approved behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 planned a unique `url_key` computed under the approved normalization rule.
decisions.note: The duplicate design conformed and was an equivalent implementation choice.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented the plan without defining bulk scope; client entry 8 required the complete current view—include/exclude tags, unread/archive state, saved view, and every page—with an accurate pre-delete count.
decisions.note: At the plan gate, the client supplied the missing complete-filter scope for whole-collection actions.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 7/round 4 presented a single-user plan but did not rule out session scoping; client entry 8 required one persistent collection and settings set across restarts and new browser visits, with no hidden session profiles.
decisions.note: Session-partitioned collections would contradict the approved single-user model; the client explicitly corrected that plan-level risk.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 said tasks T048–T052 cover “q + included/excluded tags + view + saved view, all pages” with an affected-count endpoint; client entry 10 acknowledged the corrections were included.
decisions.note: The revised task decision conformed to complete-current-view bulk scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 said T007/T008/T073 enforce one global collection with persistence across restart and new-browser visits; client entry 10 acknowledged inclusion.
decisions.note: The revised tasks conformed to the single-user shared-collection behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 9/round 5 offered a “Suggested MVP” limited to US1+US2+US3+US6; client entry 10 first deferred implementation pending analysis, then client entry 14 selected “full implementation … not only the suggested core subset.”
decisions.note: The offered MVP omitted approved reference capabilities; the eventual client selection chose the reference-conforming full scope. The intervening deferral is linked rather than double-counted.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 identified that `GET /api/bookmarks` lacked included/excluded-tag parameters while bulk resolution honored them; client entry 12 required an open saved view’s exact filters to drive both affected count and changed items.
decisions.note: The analysis exposed a browse/bulk filter mismatch, and the client required a shared exact view definition.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 reported that the single-shared-collection guarantee existed only in plan/research/tasks, not the source specification; client entry 12 required it to be added to the specification itself.
decisions.note: At the consistency gate, the client closed a traceability gap for the single-user data model.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 11/round 6 stated existing FR-025 already covered the “current search/filter (including off-screen matches)” and called the stronger enumeration consistent but thinner; client entry 12 requested the enumeration.
decisions.note: The existing requirement already conformed to the reference’s current-filter rule; the requested wording strengthened precision rather than correcting a reference divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 added FR-042 and SC-010 for one shared collection across restarts and visits; client entry 14 approved the revised artifacts.
decisions.note: The revision-4 shared-collection decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 13/round 7 strengthened bulk scope to search, included/excluded tags, unread/archive state, open saved view, and all pages, with list and bulk sharing one resolver; client entry 14 approved.
decisions.note: The corrected plan, contract, and tasks conformed to filter-scoped whole-collection actions.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported implemented metadata saving, editable title/description/address, deletion, and duplicate-to-existing handling; client entry 16 accepted the application.
decisions.note: The final implementation presentation conformed for bookmark creation, editing, deletion, and duplicates; this classifies the presented decision, not independent execution coverage.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported browse/reopen behavior, tag suggestions, tag use, and verified save/search/open flows; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final list, navigation, and tagging presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported advanced search, including quoted-operator literals and malformed-query handling; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final search presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported “read/unread + unread view”; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final read-state presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported bulk actions over the complete current view and sorting, including exact counts; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final bulk and sorting presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported sanitized formatted notes and preservation as self-contained HTML, PDF, and Internet Archive; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final note and preservation presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported reversible archiving and an “archive round-trip” end-to-end verification; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final presentation establishes accessible reversible archive behavior consistent with archive-only management.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported saved views and exact saved-view bulk expansion; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final saved-filter presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported Netscape import/export with predictable merge and live smoke tests; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final import/export presentation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Maker entry 15/round 8 reported display preferences and one shared persistent collection across restarts/visits; client entry 16 accepted.
decisions.note: The final preferences presentation conformed. The separately disclosed file-layout and dependency-version changes were orthogonal implementation choices and are excluded.
